overview: The Sui dynasty reunited China after three centuries of division, creating institutions that the Tang would inherit and perfect. Its ambitious building projects and military campaigns exhausted the state, leading to its rapid collapse.

items.text: The Grand Canal completed, connecting the Yellow River and Yangzi River systems for grain transport.
Standardization of coinage, weights and measures across the reunified empire.
Buddhism receives imperial patronage; the emperor styled himself as a Buddhist universal monarch.
Civil service examinations revived to recruit officials based on Confucian learning.
The Grand Canal remained China's main north-south transport artery for over a thousand years.

fall.text: Emperor Yang's disastrous Korean campaigns and excessive building projects led to widespread rebellion; he was assassinated by his own guards in 618.
